CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #16 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. To identify an instrument we give its name, its community and (1 mark)
   A. how it is played
   B. the colour of the shop
   C. the name of the shop
   D. its price

2. Why do we collect only dead or fallen twigs? (1 mark)
   A. To protect the environment and living trees
   B. Because they are wet
   C. Because they are heavier
   D. Because they are green

3. If the skin of a drum is loose, the sound is (1 mark)
   A. louder than a tight skin always
   B. higher
   C. lower
   D. the same as a tight skin

4. When accompanying singers, the drummers should (1 mark)
   A. shout the words
   B. stop at every line
   C. play softly enough for the singers to be heard
   D. play as loud as possible

5. Where must a player stand to shoot at goal? (1 mark)
   A. At the centre circle
   B. Inside the goal circle
   C. Anywhere on the court
   D. Behind the goal post

6. Who stops the game with a whistle for a rule break? (1 mark)
   A. The goal keeper
   B. The shooter
   C. The umpire
   D. The spectator

7. How high is the goal ring above the ground? (1 mark)
   A. 1.5 metres
   B. 10 metres
   C. 5 metres
   D. 3.05 metres

8. The first step of tying an overhand knot is to (1 mark)
   A. wet the cord
   B. make a loop
   C. burn the cord
   D. cut the cord

9. Red mixed with yellow makes (1 mark)
   A. green
   B. orange
   C. purple
   D. brown

10. What is the theme of the montage in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Weather
   B. Wild animals
   C. Food
   D. Ball games

11. What is a palette? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of brush
   B. A frame
   C. A type of paper
   D. A surface for mixing paint

12. Which is an improvised glue? (1 mark)
   A. Paint thinner
   B. Salt water
   C. Flour paste
   D. Engine oil

13. Which of these letters has neither an ascender nor a descender? (1 mark)
   A. b
   B. a
   C. d
   D. p

14. A monotone line in music writing is (1 mark)
   A. a very loud note
   B. a five-line staff
   C. a single line on which notes are written
   D. a colour

15. To compose a rhythm means to (1 mark)
   A. erase a pattern
   B. create a new pattern
   C. copy a friend's pattern exactly
   D. play an instrument only

16. Why is a pattern with only taa taa taa taa dull? (1 mark)
   A. It has too many rests
   B. It has no variation of note values
   C. It has no beat
   D. It is too long

17. How can you make a slab of even thickness? (1 mark)
   A. Drop it on the floor
   B. Squeeze with one hand
   C. Freeze it
   D. Roll the clay with a bottle between two sticks of equal thickness

18. Stepwise motion means the tune moves (1 mark)
   A. to the next note above or below
   B. by big jumps
   C. only on one note
   D. down only

19. The recorder notes G, A and B match the sol-fa syllables (1 mark)
   A. r, m and d
   B. m, r and d
   C. d, r and m
   D. m, d and r

20. How many notes are in the melody d r m m r d? (1 mark)
   A. Six
   B. Five
   C. Four
   D. Three

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how to make a ball using the macramé technique and overhand knots. (5 marks)

22. Why should a composed rhythm be your own idea? (2 marks)

23. Identify the kayamba and the drum by giving the name, the community or area and the way of playing for each. (4 marks)

24. How do you care for a paint brush? (3 marks)

25. How many beats are there in the pattern ta-te ta-te taa taa? Show your working. (3 marks)

26. Why do singers use hand signs? (2 marks)

27. Give one example of a melodic percussion instrument and one non-melodic percussion instrument. (2 marks)

28. Describe how to paint a fruit so that it looks round using colour value. (4 marks)

29. How can you show that you have identified the pitch of a note by ear? (3 marks)

30. What is a montage? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #16 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — how it is played
   Identifying uses name, community and method of playing.

2. A — To protect the environment and living trees
   Cutting living trees harms the environment.

3. C — lower
   A loose skin vibrates more slowly, so the sound is lower.

4. C — play softly enough for the singers to be heard
   Accompaniment supports the singers and must not cover their voices.

5. B — Inside the goal circle
   Shots must be taken from inside the goal circle.

6. C — The umpire
   Umpires control the game and blow the whistle.

7. D — 3.05 metres
   The netball goal ring is 3.05 metres high.

8. B — make a loop
   You make a loop first, pass the end through it and pull tight.

9. B — orange
   Red and yellow together give orange.

10. D — Ball games
   The montage is themed ball games.

11. D — A surface for mixing paint
   A palette is where paints are mixed.

12. C — Flour paste
   Flour mixed with water and heated water makes a paste.

13. B — a
   The letter a sits between the baseline and the top of small letters.

14. C — a single line on which notes are written
   On a monotone we write the rhythm on one line.

15. B — create a new pattern
   Composing is creating something original.

16. B — It has no variation of note values
   A good pattern mixes different note values.

17. D — Roll the clay with a bottle between two sticks of equal thickness
   Equal sticks on both sides keep the slab even.

18. A — to the next note above or below
   Steps go to a neighbouring note.

19. C — d, r and m
   If G is doh, then A is ray and B is me.

20. A — Six
   Count d, r, m, m, r, d to get six.

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a firm core from paper or cloth. Cut equal cords. Tie them together with an overhand knot at the middle. Put the core on top. Tie overhand knots between pairs of neighbouring cords to make a net around the core. Gather the cords at the bottom and tie a strong knot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five clear stages.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Copying is not fair and honest. Your own idea shows integrity and creativity.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Kayamba: coastal people such as the Mijikenda, played by shaking. Drum (ngoma): found in many communities, played with hands or sticks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct name, community or area and method, up to 4.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rinse when changing colour, wash with soap after use, shape the tip and store it flat or with hairs up. Never leave it standing on its hairs in water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 beats. Ta-te is 1 beat, ta-te is 1 beat, taa is 1 beat and taa is 1 beat, so 1+1+1+1 = 4.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: To show and remember the height of each note, and to help them sing in tune.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for showing pitch, 1 mark for remembering or singing in tune.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Melodic: xylophone. Non-melodic: shaker, kayamba or claves.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the outline. Paint the main colour. Add a lighter tone on the side facing the light and a darker tone on the side away from the light. Blend the edges and add a shadow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the note, decide if it is low, middle or high, and make the hand sign for it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for listening, 1 mark for deciding pitch, 1 mark for hand sign.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: A picture made by joining many cut pictures or pieces of material on a background.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for many pieces, 1 mark for joined on a background.
